rows.source_locator: renal medullary architecture and urine concentration
rows.passage_en: Juxtamedullary nephrons have loops extending deeply into the renal medulla. Their participation in the medullary countercurrent system helps mammals produce urine more concentrated than body fluids.
rows.review_note: Indexed physiological review establishes renal medulla, loops and collecting ducts; full source passage identifying juxtamedullary nephrons still needs access. The question asks can, not every mammal always concentrates urine.

rows.passage_en: Influenza is an RNA virus that replicates its genetic material and makes viral proteins after entry and uncoating in a host cell. It does not use a DNA intermediate produced by reverse transcriptase.
rows.review_note: CDC replication and host-cell entry passages directly read. “Immediately” in prompt compresses entry/uncoating/nuclear import; none of the other offered retroviral/destructive alternatives correctly describes its replication program. Need inspect RNA-virus classification passage in final pass.

rows.source_locator: Summary: The Origin and Evolution of Cells
rows.passage_en: A common model of early cell origins begins with self-replicating molecules enclosed by a lipid membrane. Nuclei and mitochondria are later features of eukaryotic cells.
rows.review_note: Indexed author textbook summary explicitly states enclosure ofRNAinphospholipid membrane; full page blocked. This supports a model-based most-likely ordering, not direct observation of the first cell.

rows.passage_en: In an ideal randomly mating population without forces maintaining associations, recombination reduces linkage disequilibrium across generations. Clonal reproduction and selection favoring particular allele combinations can preserve or create such associations.
rows.review_note: Indexed review gives D_next=(1-c)D; this does not mean random mating instantly eliminates LD or forbids drift/selection from generating it. Epistasis alone without selection does not necessarily generate LD: final option-interpretation review needed.

rows.passage_en: Primary succession begins on a newly exposed substrate that lacks an established soil community, such as bare rock or glacial deposits. Secondary succession begins where a previous community has been disturbed but soil remains.
rows.review_note: Official curriculum source explicitly defines primary succession as removal of soil/organisms leaving bare rock,gravel,silt,sand. No claim all bare substrates necessarily follow one fixed sequence.
